rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the rejected_alternative's 'than the range's thinner one-token catchword pairs' is banned, non-verse-anchored file-order phrasing. OL (high): the row's proverb_cluster rationale for 14:12-13 omits that 14:12 is byte-identical to Prov.16.25 elsewhere in the book, where the same line stands as a fully self-contained proverb sharing zero content tokens with either neighbor -- undercutting the row's central claim that the shared hinge-word is why 14:12 needs 14:13 to be complete.
rulings.grounds: Two distinct defects, both real; the OL item is upheld on substance but refined on scope/remedy. (1) Register: confirmed verbatim, non-verse-anchored ('the range's thinner one-token catchword pairs' names no verse). (2) Seam substance: independently re-verified -- oshb:Prov.14.12 and oshb:Prov.16.25 are FULL-VERSE BYTE-IDENTICAL (direct string comparison, cantillation included), and at 16:25's own location its neighbors Prov.16.24 and Prov.16.26 share ZERO skeleton-tier content tokens with it (independently re-derived token-set comparison), confirming the MT reuses this exact line as a standalone proverb elsewhere with no dependent partner. This is real, undisclosed, byte-grounded counter-evidence to the row's 'operative hinge-word' argument. It does NOT by itself prove the 14:12/14:13 pairing is spurious at 14:12's own location (the same line can function differently in different redactional contexts, and the shared hinge-word 'וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ'/'וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ' -- word-bound in both verses, root sweep = 13 verses book-wide, independently confirmed -- plus the shared appearance-vs-outcome structure are independent grounds the row also already offers), so REFINE rather than straight uphold: the defect is a disclosure and confidence-calibration failure, not proof the boundary call is wrong. Any reversion to single_proverb is a boundary change and a PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit boss adoption per book_strategy Prov.md sec6.
rulings.remedy: (a) Verse-anchor the rejected_alternative language (class-level register sweep). (b) Disclose the Prov.16.25 duplicate as counter-evidence in device_notes/rejected_alternative and add it to boundary_evidence_refs (it is argued in prose outside the row's own span -- check_refs_mirror.py's rule). (c) Re-examine confidence: either lower from medium to medium_low, or retain medium only if the structural (appearance-vs-outcome) argument is elevated to an independently named ground alongside the hinge-word, not resting on the hinge-word alone. Test: check_refs_mirror.py shows Prov.16.25 in boundary_evidence_refs; citation_sweep.py passes on the revised row; any boundary-change proposal is flagged for the boss round, not applied unilaterally.
